texts: Cafe in the Clouds - Coorg, India - Perched at 5,000 feet in the "Scotland of India," this mountaintop cafe sits inside a former British colonial tea estate barn where visitors siparabica grown on-site while watching mist roll across endless coffee plantations from uncovered HayBarn-style windows.

The Anchor Coffee House - Wellington, New Zealand - Tucked into a converted 1930s maritime radio station on a windy harbor pier, this shop serves flat white made with beans roasted in a decommissioned shipping container, where baristas compete in annual latte art throwdowns using the port's salt air as their secret ingredient.

Ca Phe Trung (Egg Coffee) - Hanoi, Vietnam - Hidden in a 1950s colonial French villa's cramped back room, this legendary spot serves the city's original egg coffee—whipped egg yolk mixed with condensed milk and robusta espresso—poured tableside from brass Vietnamese phin filters in a recipe invented here during wartime milk shortages when fresh dairy was unavailable.
